To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pharmacokinetics of long-acting antiretroviral drugs can be modelled in children and adolescents and that the optimal doses for children and adolescents are predicted using physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling.
we developed a physiologically based pharmacokinetic model for children and adolescents and we identified the optimal dose of long acting injectable antiretovirals in children and adolescents.
we used physiologically-based models to predict dosing strategies for long-acting antiretrovirials in children and adolescents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of physiologically-based modelling and simulation approaches to support the design and optimisation of long-acting formulations in children and adolescent populations.
the development of physiologically-based modelling and simulation approaches to predict the pharmacokinetics of long-acting antiretrovirials in children and adolescents.
the development of a physiologically-based model to predict the pharmacokinetics of long-acting antiretrovirials cabotegravir (CAB-LA) and rilpiverine (RPV-LA) in children and adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed dosing strategies are a rational starting point for the design of future clinical studies in children and adults.
the optimal doses of cabotegrivar and rilpivrinar for long-acting intramuscular injection in children and adolescents were identified using a physiologically-based modelling approach.

the optimal dose of monthly administration of long-acting cabotegravir was 100–200 mg and 150–300 mg for children aged 2–6 years and 7–12 years, respectively, while the optimal dose of rilpivinir was 250–500 mg for children and adolescents aged 3–18 years, to achieve trough plasma concentration above the target concentrations derived from a recent efficacy trial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal dose for long-acting cabotegravir in children and adolescents would be 200-600 mg loading dose and 100-250 mg maintenance dose, and for long-acting rilpivrine in children and adolescents 250-550 mg loading dose, and 150-500 mg maintenance dose.
the proposed methodology can provide a valuable tool for the identification of dosing strategies for long-acting antiretrovirais in children and adolescents.
the physiologically based modelling approach is a valuable tool to identify potential doses of long-actin antiretroviral formulations in children and adolescent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
long-acting injectables are a feasible alternative for children and adolescents, and that the dose should be tailored to the weight of the patient.
the dose of long-acting formulations of antiretrovirials should be weight-based, and that the loading dose should be administered in the first month.
, in the absence of clinical data, physiologically-based modelling can be used to inform dosing strategies for long-acting antiretroviral agents in children and adolescents.
